property_summary: For any call to onERC721Received that does not revert, the return value must equal ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector (0x150b7a02); the bug returns 0xFFFFFFFF instead.
After `initialize`, the `baseToken` state variable must equal the `_baseToken` argument passed to `initialize`; the mutant incorrectly sets it to `address(0)`.
After initialization, the baseToken state variable must equal the _baseToken parameter that was passed to initialize; the mutant sets it to _nft instead, violating this invariant.
After initialization, baseToken must equal the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant sets it to address(this) instead, violating this equality.
After initialization, state variable nft must equal the _nft parameter; the bug sets it to _baseToken instead, so reading nft() yields a different value.
After initialization, the public nft state variable must match the _nft parameter; the bug sets nft to address(0) regardless of the provided _nft.
After calling initialize, the public getter nft() returns the address passed as the _nft parameter, but the mutant never assigns nft, so it stays address(0).

After initialization, the changeFee state variable must equal the _changeFee parameter passed to initialize; the bug sets it to 0 regardless, so for any non-zero _changeFee, the stored changeFee differs.
After initialization, the stored changeFee must equal the _changeFee argument passed; the bug leaves changeFee at zero regardless of the argument.
After successful initialization, the feeRate must not exceed 5000 (5%), but the mutant allows any feeRate to be stored.
After initialization, feeRate must equal the _feeRate argument passed; the bug deletes that assignment, so feeRate always stays 0.

initialize() must revert only when _feeRate > 5000; the mutant reverts when _feeRate <= 5000, so after a successful call the stored feeRate is never > 5000 in the reference but may be > 5000 in the mutant.
After a successful initialize call, the stored feeRate must never exceed 5000, but the mutant allows feeRate > 5000 to be stored.
After initialization, the stored feeRate must equal the supplied _feeRate parameter, but the mutant doubles it, causing feeRate() != _feeRate.
After a successful initialize() call with any _feeRate <= 5000, the feeRate state variable must equal the supplied _feeRate; the buggy version ignores the supplied value and sets feeRate to 10000.
